subject: Agriculture
title: Drainage and Waterlogging
description: A 60-second lesson on Drainage and Waterlogging.

hook.text: Too little water kills crops. Too much water also kills them—by drowning their roots.

buildup.text: Waterlogged soil has no air in its pores. Roots can't breathe, and anaerobic bacteria produce toxic compounds.

discovery.text: Tile drainage—perforated pipes buried underground—lowers the water table and keeps roots in the aerated zone.

twist.text: Drainage works too well sometimes. It flushes nitrates into rivers, causing algal blooms downstream.

climax.text: Modern controlled drainage uses adjustable outlets to hold water when needed and release it when necessary.

punchline.text: Drainage saves crops—but what drains away matters too.

quiz.question: Why is waterlogged soil harmful to crops?
options: Roots can't access oxygen and toxic compounds build up
